title: Maximum Equal Frequency
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> count(100001): frequency of each value → O(V)
- vector<int> freq(100001): count of values at each frequency → O(V)
- not counted: input nums, returned int
approach: Iterate left to right, maintaining `count[x]` (occurrences of value `x`), `freq[f]` (how many distinct values currently have frequency `f`), and `maxFreq`. After adding element `i` (prefix length `len = i+1`), the prefix is "good" iff one of three shapes holds: (A) `maxFreq == 1` (delete any one, all remaining appear once); (B) exactly one value appears once and all others appear `maxFreq` times - delete the singleton, so `freq[1]==1 && freq[maxFreq]*maxFreq == len-1`; (C) exactly one value appears `maxFreq` times and all others appear `maxFreq-1` times - delete one copy of the max-freq value, so `freq[maxFreq]==1 && (freq[maxFreq-1]+1)*(maxFreq-1) == len-1`. Take the largest `len` that is good.
hints: After deleting one element, what must be true about how many times each remaining value appears? The array length can be up to 10^5.

Keep two arrays: `count[x]` = occurrences of value `x`, and `freq[f]` = how many distinct values currently have frequency `f`, plus running `maxFreq`. At prefix length 7 of Example 1 we have `freq={2:3, 1:1}`, `maxFreq=2`: one singleton (5) to delete, the other three values all at frequency 2.

```
for each x at index i (len = i+1):
    decrement freq[count[x]], increment count[x], increment freq[count[x]]
    update maxFreq
    good = (maxFreq == 1)
          or (freq[1]==1 and freq[maxFreq]*maxFreq == len-1)
          or (freq[maxFreq]==1 and (freq[maxFreq-1]+1)*(maxFreq-1) == len-1)
    if good: ans = len
return ans
```

**All elements equal** - a single distinct value repeated.
`Input: nums = [1,1,1]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: omitting Case C (one value at maxFreq, delete one of its copies) → returns 2.

**All distinct** - every value appears exactly once.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4]` → `Expected: 4`
⚠️ Bug: not treating `maxFreq == 1` as valid → returns 0.

**Two copies of one value** - smallest non-trivial prefix.
`Input: nums = [1,1]` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: Case C check using `freq[maxFreq-1]*(maxFreq-1)` instead of `(freq[maxFreq-1]+1)*(maxFreq-1)` → returns 1.

**Singleton plus uniform block** - one outlier to delete.
`Input: nums = [1,1,2,2,3]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: Case B check using `freq[maxFreq]*maxFreq == len` instead of `== len-1` → returns 0.

followUps.q: What if nums arrives as an unbounded stream you cannot store?
followUps.a: Process each element online, keeping only `count` and `freq` maps plus `maxFreq`; the three goodness checks are O(1) per element. Time stays O(n) expected, space O(U) where U is distinct values seen so far.

followUps.q: What if you must remove exactly k elements instead of 1?
followUps.a: Generalize the checks: after removing k, all remaining values share frequency f, so the frequency-of-frequencies distribution must be collapsible by subtracting k total from the top end. This needs examining a few candidate f values around maxFreq, giving O(n) per check but more cases; overall O(n) with careful counting.

followUps.q: What if nums[i] can be up to 10^9 (or negative)?
followUps.a: Replace the fixed-size `count` array with an `unordered_map<int,int>` keyed by value; `freq` can stay an array indexed by frequency (still ≤ n). Time O(n) expected, space O(n).
